messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/generate (dedicated-pool-east-2). Impact=customer-facing SLO breach. Alerting oncall-ops.

oncall-ops: got it, tuning in. pulling up dashboards. p95 also creeping up.

javier: I'm seeing sustained queue_depth ~1200 across pool-3, target capacity 10 GPUs, active 10. autoscaler didn't add workers; last scale event failed with warmup_timeout.

sarah: confirmed streaming stalls in traces — chunked SSE connections report stalls at token 2-5s sometimes. tail latency heavy.

mike: reproducing with local loadtester: short payloads (avg 110 tokens) high rps burst. KV cache misses are high on cold nodes (miss rate ~0.86).

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (dedicated saturation + autoscale delay). Severity: Sev2. Runbook: dedicated-saturation -> warmup -> manual-scale.

oncall-ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) manual add GPU nodes (warm) 2) route burst to hosted fallback model 3) apply temporary rate limit to non-critical customers. Thoughts?

javier: manual add in-progress. spun up 4 nodes but warmup is slow because quantized kernels JIT on first requests. We can pre-warm by sending model init priming calls.

sarah: starting pre-warm script against the new instances (priv infra). snippet: ```bash
for ip in $(cat new_nodes.txt); do curl -s -X POST http://$ip:8080/init -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","seq":128}'; done
```

mike: while warming, let's reduce concurrency per worker to reduce head-of-line blocking. Patch rolling out to runtime config: `max_concurrency_per_gpu: 12 -> 8` (apply to pool-3 only). This should lower p99 for streaming.

emily-cs: customer-impact: 3 enterprise customers reported degraded streaming UX (timeouts, partial responses). CS is sending interim comms.

alenia: autoscaler log shows `scale_event_timeout: 60s` and nodes stuck in `provisioning -> configuring` for ~90s. Looks like cloud image bootstrap scripts hit an apt lock due to concurrent package installs.

oncall-ops: ack. change of plan: 1) increase autoscaler timeout to 300s to avoid premature abort 2) fix bootstrap concurrency (serialize apt-get or use pre-baked AMI) 3) manually scale to absorb current queue.

javier: manual scale done: +4 nodes added to pool-3, queue_depth dropping from 1200 -> 320 in ~2m, p95 improving but p99 still elevated (~2.5s -> 1.1s p95, p99 ~3.8s).

sarah: streaming stalls resolved on most traces after pre-warm. remaining p99 tails are from requests that hit nodes still compiling kernels. we should pin models to already-compiled variants during rollouts.

mike: rolling config to prefer cached model variant: `preferred_variant: quantized-int8-cached` for 10m window. deploying now.

ops-bot: Note: temporary routing rule created: route bursts > 120rps for single-customer to hosted-fallback.

emily-cs: customers A and B moved to fallback, response times back to normal for them. Customer C requested SLA credit — flagging for billing/product.

alenia: root cause summary so far: autoscaler timeout + bootstrap races -> slow warmup -> high queue depths; cold-start kernel JIT causing per-request tail latency; workload characteristics (high short-burst traffic) amplified queueing.

oncall-ops: continuing monitoring. action items: (A) extend autoscaler timeout + pre-baked images (ops) (B) add pre-warm probe + automatic init calls when new nodes register (runtime) (C) fallback routing policy and per-customer throttles (platform) (D) evaluate kernel-compile background threads to avoid blocking first request (infra/ml).

javier: documenting commands used to scale/manually pre-warm for runbook: ```bash
# scale
redwood-cli pool scale --pool pool-3 --add 4
# pre-warm
xargs -a new_nodes.txt -I{} curl -s http://{}:8080/init -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","seq":256}' &
```

sarah: updating status page: "We are investigating increased latency for dedicated capacity in us-east-2; routing mitigations in place."

oncall-ops: handing off to next oncall @mike in 30m for follow-up and post-incident actions. please keep thread updated.

mike: ack, will own postmortem + action tracking. initial timeline: detect -> scale -> pre-warm -> reroute -> stable (approx 15m).

emily-cs: CS to follow up with affected customers and provide timeline and mitigation notes.

oj: (minutes later, ops-bot automated update) autoscaler metrics: median provisioning time now 45s (after config), mean kernel compile time 18s, background compile queue length 0.

mike: closing incident channel for active mitigation; keeping thread for follow-ups. please file a postmortem doc and link here.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 transitioned to "mitigated". Postmortem requested in 72h.

mike: Postmortem owners: mike, javier, alenia. Draft ETA 72h. Immediate remediation tickets created: OPS-342 (pre-baked images), RUNTIME-217 (auto pre-warm probe), SCALE-88 (increase autoscaler timeout and better retry), PLATFORM-190 (fallback routing rules).

emily-cs: adding customer notes to CS tracker. closing updates unless any regressions. :white_check_mark:
